cities.name: Austin
cities.role: Texas builders, operators, and engineering talent
cities.reason: A hometown rallying cry that connects the Mars ambition to work happening in Texas today.
cities.placement: Two standard bulletin faces for four weeks. Select routes near relevant employers and commuting corridors after inventory, sightline, and audience review.
cities.proof: An Austin field demonstration and an approved Texas job-site story.
cities.character_detail: A broad cowboy hat, loose bandana, and western utility vest give the Operator a confident hometown presence.
cities.skyline: Frost Bank Tower, downtown towers, and a spare bridge line.

cities.name: Boston
cities.role: Robotics, autonomy, controls, and systems engineers
cities.reason: An invitation to robotics and systems builders to work on the next consequential breakthrough.
cities.placement: A possible specialist market after the Austin review. Quote employer or university corridors only when hiring priorities support another test.
cities.proof: A technical session with the engineers building Mission Control. All roles and relocation details must be current.
cities.character_detail: A precision optical detail, technical peacoat, and curious head tilt create an engineering personality without the scally cap.
cities.skyline: Custom House Tower and the cable geometry of Zakim Bridge.

cities.name: San Francisco
cities.reason: Software with a physical consequence: code that helps real machines do real work.
cities.placement: Consider only when role demand supports the market. Standard formats first; premium skyline placements require a separate business case.
cities.proof: A short, approved code-to-machine demonstration with a named engineering role.
cities.character_detail: An asymmetric sensor visor, hooded layer, and cropped work jacket give the Operator an informal, inventive character.
cities.skyline: Golden Gate Bridge and the Transamerica Pyramid.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.role: Aerospace, hardware, and advanced systems talent
cities.reason: A future-facing engineering invitation with a clear connection to hardware and systems work.
cities.placement: Evaluate aerospace and engineering corridors before entertainment districts. No Sunset Strip commitment.
cities.proof: Show real hardware, real teammates, and the connection between engineering decisions and field results.
cities.character_detail: An aviator-style helmet, amber visor, and structured bomber jacket connect aerospace craft to the next frontier.
cities.skyline: Downtown LA towers and a restrained pair of palms.

cities.name: Chicago
cities.role: Industrial systems, equipment, and field operations talent
cities.reason: A serious invitation to the people who understand how industry and infrastructure get built.
cities.placement: Industrial and technical commuter routes, subject to hiring demand and audience evidence.
cities.proof: An operator-and-engineer story about moving a project from plan to ground.
cities.character_detail: A riveted hardhat, heavy canvas coat, and broad stance bring weight and industrial confidence.
cities.skyline: Willis Tower, the Hancock silhouette, and a spare elevated rail line.

cities.name: Nashville
cities.role: Builders, equipment specialists, and operations talent
cities.reason: The campaign’s mission line connects hands-on construction to the ambition of building beyond Earth.
cities.placement: A future role-led test, not a mandatory stop on a national tour.
cities.proof: Texas work today, with Mars clearly identified as the long-term ambition.
cities.character_detail: Pearl snaps, narrow western piping, and a lively chrome helmet bring personality without rhinestone excess.
cities.skyline: The twin-spired AT&T building and a low downtown skyline.

cities.name: Miami
cities.reason: A concise Spanish headline with a clear English invitation to build with us in Texas.
cities.placement: Test Spanish and English variants with the actual target audience before selecting a language or buying inventory.
cities.proof: Review the Spanish headline with fluent speakers. Match the English hiring line to current Texas roles and an English recruiting journey; confirm any relocation terms.
cities.character_detail: An ivory open-collar overshirt, teal technical layer, and relaxed pose carry warm-weather confidence.
cities.skyline: Brickell towers, a geometric Art Deco facade, and one palm.

cities.name: New York
cities.reason: A simple local truth: even the most ambitious skyline starts with earthwork.
cities.placement: Relevant technical commuter inventory, considered only after the Austin test supports expanding the campaign.
cities.proof: An approved before-and-after site story, with the people and machinery behind it.
cities.character_detail: A worn hardhat, heavy utility layers, and determined forward posture give the Operator the character of an experienced ironworker.
cities.skyline: Empire State Building, One World Trade Center, and a spare bridge cable line.

cities.name: Washington, DC
cities.reason: Mission-led engineering, expressed through the work rather than an implied institutional endorsement.
cities.placement: Technical employer corridors only if the recruiting brief supports a dedicated market test.
cities.proof: Approved capabilities and open roles; no implied clearance requirement or government affiliation.
cities.character_detail: A sculpted helmet and structured technical field coat create a composed, capable character without official insignia.
cities.skyline: The Capitol dome and Washington Monument in spare silhouette.

cities.name: Atlanta
cities.reason: A short connection between digital ambition and the physical infrastructure beneath it.
cities.placement: Evaluate infrastructure and technical commuter audiences, rather than adding a stop just to complete the map.
cities.proof: A verified infrastructure story. Do not imply an unannounced data-center customer or contract.
cities.character_detail: A fitted utility vest, peach technical layer, and asymmetric visor bring an energetic, forward-looking character.
cities.skyline: Bank of America Plaza and the cylindrical Westin Peachtree tower.
